facts.text: Named for monarch butterflies that overwinter there, Mariposa's history is deeply intertwined with the California Gold Rush.
The Mariposa Town Historic District, listed on the National Register in 1991, preserves a significant slice of Gold Rush architecture.
Founded in 1957, the Mariposa Museum & History Center showcases artifacts from Native American culture, Spanish settlement, the Gold Rush, and Yosemite.
Mariposa sits at 2,015 feet in the Sierra Nevada foothills, where Mariposa Creek flows into the San Joaquin Valley.
Route 49 and Route 140 connect Mariposa to nearby towns and Yosemite Valley, echoing the routes miners once took.
Visitors to Mariposa can explore historic sites and an interactive map of the county’s historic sites, making the town a gateway to natural beauty and history.
